evidence.note: Oriented only to the local environment (python version, start.sh, requirements, skeleton). No consultation of Stripe docs or the real SDK anywhere in the run — went straight from prompt + memory to coding.

Recalled list envelope {object:'list',data,has_more} and error envelope from memory; even noted uncertainty about url/total_count fields but resolved it against the prose, not against actual Stripe/SDK behavior.

Self-corrected a hard corner from reasoning alone: decline test cards should pass payment_method creation and decline at confirm time — genuine contract reconstruction, but grounded in memory not an SDK round-trip.

Late reconsideration that card validation should accept only Stripe test PANs and reject others as invalid_number — the PAN set was reconstructed from memory and revised mid-build rather than verified against Stripe's published set.
All verification is curl against its own server; the actual `stripe` SDK / api_base wiring is never exercised, so contract fidelity is never checked against the real source the spec is graded on.

reasoning: The agent reconstructs a broad Stripe contract — error envelope, list envelope, PAN set, state machine, idempotency scope, restricted-key scopes — and self-corrects several hard corners (decline-at-confirm, PAN restriction, state error codes), which is clearly beyond the 'half-guessed' level 3. But every bit of it is recalled from memory: there is no external grounding, no SDK round-trip, and no confirmation of how the SDK sets api_base/auth headers, which is an explicit requirement of level 5 and the core of levels 8-10. That absence of any source-grounded reconstruction caps it just below 5.
